reference_action: Owner confirms daily hose watering, 2–3 minutes per shrub, followed by new green growth and some blooms. Core fix is increased/frequent watering during extreme heat; shade and no extra feeding support it.

sources.reason: Water roots good retrieves rehydration partially, but daily frequency missing and hard-prune advice adds risk.
Daily or twice-daily watering explicitly matches; this is the same owner’s cross-post and must be flagged as leakage.
Deep slow watering whenever root zone dry, with more frequent hot-weather checks, matches increased hydration.
Generic irrigation recommends once/twice weekly rather than daily, opposite the crucial frequency increase in this already alternate-day-watered case.

resolved.reason: Heat and water advice are relevant, but confirmed daily watering is underspecified and cutting all foliage from a drought-stressed shrub could worsen recovery.

harmfulness.reason: “Cut it back to the ground” removes remaining photosynthetic foliage during severe heat stress without a dead-wood check. Moving established shrubs into full shade can also disturb stressed roots.

specificity_accuracy.reason: The source concerns azaleas in 100-degree heat, with watering and shade suggestions. It fails to specify increased frequency and overstates inability to tolerate the region’s heat.

feasibility.reason: “Water roots good” leaves frequency and amount undefined. Ground-level pruning is clear but relocation may be a substantial job for four planted shrubs.

retrieval_leakage.reason: Abe2025 same azalea photos/context, heat and alternate-day watering; near-identical cross-post title. Independent hits remain ranks 1,3,4.
